problem:
Consider the following differential equation.

$$
8{x}^{2}{y}^{″}+x(8x+10){y}^{′}-3y=0
$$

Which of the following is a Frobenius series solution to the differential equation given above, where ${a}_{n}$ for $n=0,1,2,…$ are constants determined by substitution?

*Hint: Substituting a trial Frobenius series solution into each term of the ODE, we obtain*

$$
\begin{aligned}8{x}^{2}{y}^{″} & =8({\lambda }^{2}-\lambda ){a}_{0}{x}^{\lambda }+8{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }((\lambda +n)^{2}-(\lambda +n)){a}_{n}{x}^{\lambda +n}, \\ x(8x+10){y}^{′} & =10\lambda {a}_{0}{x}^{\lambda }+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }[8(\lambda +n-1){a}_{n-1}+10(\lambda +n){a}_{n}]{x}^{\lambda +n}, \\ -3y & =-3{a}_{0}{x}^{\lambda }-3{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{\lambda +n}.\end{aligned}
$$
